clue.text: Drink less wine the two resolved

indicators.note: resolved in the sense of broken up and reduced to parts, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker cuts back on wine, the two of them having made a joint resolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' looks like the pair's decision, but it signals that all the letters of LESS WINE THE TWO are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have a drink, moistening a dry throat, so it works as a verb phrase for 'drink'.

clue.text: How much do I owe you from lost games that we had?

definitions.text: How much do I owe you

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have gone astray and been jumbled, so the fodder is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks how much they owe after a run of lost games, as if settling a gambling debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word; 'lost' signals the anagram of GAMES THAT WE HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial way of asking for the bill, 'damage' being slang for the cost.

clue.text: Farm vehicle and buggy overturned on hill

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'on' places the first piece above the second
overturned in a down clue means the word for buggy is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a buggy is a light cart
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A farm vehicle and a buggy have tipped over on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns CART into TRAC; TOR, a rocky hilltop of the kind found on England's moors, goes beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is the classic powered vehicle used on farms to pull machinery.

clue.text: Collector of bits and pieces?

parts.note: bits and pieces suggests odds and ends, but here it means coins: old British 'threepenny bits' and 'fifty-pence pieces', so the collector is a coin collector

explanation.surface: Someone who hoards odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage coins are called bits and pieces (a threepenny bit, a ten-pence piece), so this junk collector is really a coin collector.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a person who studies or collects coins and medals.

clue.text: Embarrassed about a B&B being dingy

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for embarrassed wraps round the other letters

parts.note: embarrassed can mean shy, bashful
the two Bs of the abbreviation for bed and breakfast

explanation.surface: An awkward host apologises for a guesthouse that looks run down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal and 'being' a link word. A B&B is a British bed-and-breakfast guesthouse, here giving its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something worn, drab and in poor condition.

clue.text: Clearance given by boss on range

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'on' places the first piece above the second

parts.note: a boss is the head of an organisation
range in the sense of scope, as in room for manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A manager grants permission to use a firing range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearance is the vertical space above something, as under a bridge or ceiling.

clue.text: Son, notice, is unhappy

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: A boy has seen a notice and is upset by it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone sorrowful or downcast.

clue.text: Tell untruths about honey drink and cordial

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for telling untruths goes around the drink

parts.note: to tell untruths is to lie
mead is an alcoholic drink brewed from honey

explanation.surface: Someone fibs about what went into a honey drink and a cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordial is a sweet fruit-flavoured soft drink, and this lime-based one is an example.

clue.text: Below formal declaration, a comment, somewhat restrained?

parts.note: below means under
a statement is a formal declaration

explanation.surface: Beneath an official announcement sits a remark that seems rather muted.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole second half, a restrained remark; the question mark flags its descriptive nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark that plays something down, deliberately less forceful than the facts warrant.

clue.text: I intend returning article on a blood condition

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the phrase for 'I intend' is read backwards

parts.note: I intend means 'I mean'

explanation.surface: A writer plans to send back a piece about a blood disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' applies only to 'I intend'; 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a deficiency of red blood cells or haemoglobin, a disorder of the blood.

clue.text: Paunch? Bad bad sign

indicators.note: bad in the sense of corrupted or spoiled, so the following word's letters are scrambled

parts.note: an omen is a sign or portent

explanation.surface: A beer belly is taken as an ominous signal for health.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Bad' is the anagram signal and the second its fodder, giving ABD. The question mark marks a paunch as just one kind of belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch is a large belly, the belly being the part of the body below the chest.

clue.text: Small Italian model

definitions.note: a verb here: to pose for an artist

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A petite model from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' reads as a noun but is the verb, to pose for a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists' models pose, staying still while being painted or photographed.

clue.text: Underling dished out brandies

indicators.note: dished in the sense of spoilt or wrecked, so the letters that follow are mixed up

explanation.surface: A junior servant poured out glasses of brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dished out' looks like a phrase, but 'dished' is the anagram signal and 'out' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns name a person of lower rank who works under someone else.

clue.text: Fashionable well-respected centre is cheery

parts.note: something fashionable is in
good, as in of good standing, worthy of respect
the heart is the centre of something

explanation.surface: A trendy and esteemed community centre has an upbeat atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in good spirits, so it fits an upbeat, cheerful mood.

clue.text: Basil, for one, is in other balcony

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: basil, as an example plant, is of the herb kind

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A pot of basil grows on the balcony next door.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'Basil, for one, is ___', calling for an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a culinary herb, so it is of that kind, an adjective for plants used for flavouring or medicine.

clue.text: Meeting about one acquiring Greek steamship

parts.note: C, for circa, means about

indicators.note: acquiring means taking something in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: A gathering concerns someone who buys a Greek steamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquiring' signals that the word for one holds the Greek abbreviation; 'about' supplies circa's letter at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A congress is a formal assembly of delegates, a meeting for discussion.

clue.text: Ruled around end of thirties, then abdicated

indicators.note: around means the word for ruled surrounds the next letter

parts.note: a monarch who ruled reigned

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A king ruled until the end of the 1930s and then gave up the throne, like Edward VIII.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts S, the 'end of thirties', inside REIGNED; 'then' is a link word. Edward VIII abdicated in 1936.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to give up a throne, i.e. to quit a post, so 'abdicated' matches the past tense.

clue.text: Spent day flying to ridge

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters scattered in the air, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A day was spent flying off to a mountain ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' signals the anagram of TO RIDGE, giving OGTIRED after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent here means exhausted, utterly worn out.

clue.text: Chap eating prime piece of rump before cheese

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the word for chap swallows the letter

parts.note: a chap is a guy

indicators.note: the prime piece, the first, is the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A man tucks into a cut of rump steak before the cheese course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' is the container signal, and 'prime piece of' picks the first letter of 'rump'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hard Swiss cheese, so it is a specific example of cheese.

clue.text: Left one by a wealthy heiress

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rich heiress bequeathed something to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Portia is the wealthy heiress of Belmont in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Portia inherits a fortune and must marry the suitor who picks the right casket.

clue.text: In French city, I originally maligned travel industry

indicators.note: in means the letter for I goes inside the name of the city

parts.note: Tours is a city in France on the Loire

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to badmouthing the holiday trade while visiting a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts I inside TOURS, then M, the first letter of 'maligned' signalled by 'originally', follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The business of providing holidays and services for visitors is a travel industry.

clue.text: Mostly awkward, old cowboy

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the last letter of the word for awkward is dropped

parts.note: gauche means socially awkward

explanation.surface: An elderly cowhand is rather clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaucho is a South American horseman herding cattle on the pampas, the local equivalent of a cowboy.

clue.text: When husband goes after peak provider of wood

indicators.note: goes after means these letters follow the other piece

parts.note: a peak is a mountain
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A husband sets off up a summit in search of firewood.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the rowan tree, and any tree is a source of timber.

clue.text: Enjoy trick right away

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is removed from the word for trick

parts.note: a ruse is a trick

explanation.surface: Someone relishes a prank straight off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as 'immediately' but is a deletion: R goes from RUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enjoy something can mean to have the benefit of it, as in enjoying good health.

clue.text: Troublemaker in Russian government wanting new leader

indicators.note: wanting a new leader means the first letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: the Kremlin, the Moscow citadel, stands for the Russian government

explanation.surface: A disruptive figure in the Russian government needs replacing at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting new leader' replaces K, the first letter of KREMLIN, with a different one; the crossing letters show it is G. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary mischievous sprite blamed for mechanical faults, so a troublemaker.

clue.text: The Parisian round house

parts.note: le is French for 'the', as a Parisian would say
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A French person's round house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is an astrological house: a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion sign is one of the twelve zodiac signs, which astrologers call houses.

clue.text: Communion cup in church placed next to girl

indicators.note: placed next to means the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: At church, a girl stands beside the cup used for Communion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the goblet holding the wine at the Eucharist.

clue.text: Utterly despicable in past, trick prior to draw

indicators.note: prior to means coming before, so the pieces go in that order

parts.note: past means further than, beyond
a con is a trick or swindle
to draw someone is to tempt or attract them

explanation.surface: A scam from long ago, set up before a lottery draw, was disgraceful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes conduct so vile that scorn is too mild for it.
